'''Quinn Michael McNemar''' (February 20, 1900 – July 3, 1986)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hastorf |first1=A. H. |last2=Hilgard |first2=E. R. |last3=Sears |first3=R. R. |title=Quinn McNemar (1900–1986) |journal=American Psychologist |date=1988 |volume=43 |issue=3 |pages=196–197 |doi=10.1037/h0091955 }}</ref> was an American [[psychologist]] and [[statistician]]. He is known for his work on [[IQ tests]], for his book ''Psychological Statistics'' (1949) and for [[McNemar's test]], the statistical test he introduced in 1947.<ref name=McNemar1947>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1007/BF02295996| volume = 12| issue = 2| pages = 153–157| last = McNemar| first = Quinn| title = Note on the sampling error of the difference between correlated proportions or percentages| journal = Psychometrika| date = 1947-06-18| pmid = 20254758| s2cid = 46226024}}</ref><ref name=ST>{{cite journal|title=Quinn McNemar, reviser of IQ test|date=Spring–Summer 1986|journal=Sandstone and Tile|publisher=Stanford Historical Society|volume=10|issue=3–4|url=http://histsoc.stanford.edu/pdfST/ST10no3_4.pdf|access-date=2009-05-11|archive-date=2010-07-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100705212231/http://histsoc.stanford.edu/pdfST/ST10no3_4.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Life==
McNemar was born in [[Greenland, West Virginia]] in 1900. He obtained his bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1925 from [[Juniata College]], studied for his doctorate in psychology under [[Lewis Terman]] at [[Stanford University]], and joined the faculty at Stanford in 1931. In 1942 he published ''The Revision of the [[Stanford–Binet Scale]]'', the IQ test released in 1916 by Terman. By the time he retired from Stanford in 1965 he held professorships in psychology, statistics and education. He taught for another five years at the [[University of Texas]] before retiring to [[Palo Alto]], where he died in 1986.<ref name=ST/>

He was president of the [[Psychometric Society]] in 1951 and of the [[American Psychological Association]] in 1964.<ref>{{cite book|title=A Dictionary of Statistics|publisher=Oxford University Press|year=2008|chapter=Quinn McNemar|url=http://www.answers.com/topic/quinn-mcnemar}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Psychologists Honor Scientists at Sub Base |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/47578967/quinn-mcnemar-1900-1986/ |newspaper=The Courier-Journal |date=September 3, 1962 |page=31 |via = [[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=March 29, 2020}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Former APA Presidents |url=https://www.apa.org/about/governance/president/former-presidents |website=American Psychological Association |access-date=March 29, 2020}}</ref>
